thesis.title: Design and Evaluation of a Privacy-Preserving Self-Sovereign Identity System for Bangladesh E-Government Services
thesis.institution: Department of Computer Science and Engineering

problem_statement.summary: Bangladesh's current e-KYC system (Porichoy API) requires every verifier (banks, hospitals) to query the Election Commission's centralized database with the citizen's raw NID for every transaction.
core_problems: Mass surveillance: Government can track every transaction a citizen makes
Data leakage: Banks store raw NID copies which can be hacked or breached
Single point of failure: If EC server is down, all e-KYC in Bangladesh halts
Over-disclosure: Verifiers receive more personal data than they need

proposed_solution.name: Self-Sovereign Identity (SSI) with Decentralized Public Key Infrastructure (DPKI)
proposed_solution.core_idea: Government signs a cryptographic credential once. Citizens present selective zero-knowledge proofs. Verifiers authenticate in ~11ms without contacting any central database.
key_properties: Zero-Knowledge: NID number never leaves the citizen's device
Selective Disclosure: Citizen controls exactly which attributes to share
Unlinkability: Government cannot track where citizen uses their credential
Tamper-Evidence: Any data modification is mathematically detected
Decentralized: No single point of failure

technology_stack.blockchain: Solidity 0.8.20 smart contract on Ethereum/Polygon EVM
technology_stack.frontend: Tailwind CSS, FontAwesome, JetBrains Mono (all served from single demo_server.js)
technology_stack.did_method: did:key:nid-ssi (custom DID method for thesis PoC)

project_files.demo_server.js: All-in-one server: backend API + HTML frontend + cryptographic engine embedded. Single file to run everything.
project_files.scripts/01_crypto_engine.js: Core cryptographic library: HMAC commitments, Merkle tree, ECDSA signing, DID derivation, presentation generation, 5-point verification.
project_files.scripts/02_deploy_and_benchmark.js: Hardhat script: deploys NIDRegistry.sol to local EVM, runs full lifecycle, measures real gas costs.
project_files.scripts/03_interactive_cli.js: Terminal-based CLI demo (legacy, replaced by web UI).
project_files.contracts/NIDRegistry.sol: Ethereum smart contract: DPKI trust anchor, revocation registry, 2-of-3 guardian social recovery.
project_files.hardhat.config.js: Hardhat configuration for local EVM node.

api_endpoints.POST /api/issue: Issues a signed Verifiable Credential. Validates Bangladesh NID format (10-digit Smart or 17-digit Legacy with birth-year check). Returns Merkle root, ECDSA signature, DID.
api_endpoints.POST /api/generate-proof: Citizen generates a selective blinded presentation proof. Input: disclosedKeys array. Returns presentation token.
api_endpoints.GET /api/verify: Verifier runs 5-point cryptographic audit. Returns: valid (bool), reason, check results, latencyMs.
api_endpoints.POST /api/tamper-test: Corrupts a disclosed attribute value. Verifies Merkle proof detects the tampering.
api_endpoints.POST /api/revoke: Toggles credential revocation status (on-chain simulation). Revoked credentials fail verification.
api_endpoints.POST /api/guardian-vote: Simulates 2-of-3 guardian social recovery. Two guardian votes rotate the citizen device key.
api_endpoints.POST /api/benchmark: Runs N cryptographic cycles (default 50). Returns mean/median/p95 latency for proof generation and verification.
api_endpoints.GET /api/status: Returns full session state: credential, presentation, DID addresses, event count.
api_endpoints.GET /api/events: Returns chronological event log of all actions in current session.
api_endpoints.POST /api/reset: Resets entire server state to clean empty state.

step_1_commitment.process: For each attribute (nid, name, dob, district, isOver18): generate 32-byte random salt, compute HMAC(salt, attributeValue). Salt is stored secretly in citizen wallet.
step_1_commitment.property: Hiding - attacker cannot reverse a commitment to find the original value

step_2_merkle_tree.process: All 5 attribute commitments become Merkle leaves. Pairs are hashed together recursively until a single 32-byte Merkle Root R is produced.
step_2_merkle_tree.property: Binding - any single attribute change causes a completely different root

step_3_signature.process: Government Issuer signs Merkle Root R with their private key. Public key registered on blockchain (DPKI).
step_3_signature.property: Authenticity - only the authorized government issuer can produce a valid signature

step_4_selective_disclosure.process: Citizen reveals chosen attributes + their salts + Merkle sibling path. Verifier recomputes commitments and verifies Merkle inclusion proof against signed root R.
step_4_selective_disclosure.property: Zero-Knowledge - undisclosed attributes are mathematically provably hidden

step_5_holder_binding.process: Citizen device signs the presentation with their own ECDSA key (citizenWallet). Verifier checks this signature against citizen DID.
step_5_holder_binding.property: Holder Binding - only the rightful credential owner can generate a valid presentation

functions.constructor: Sets deployer as authorized Government Issuer, stores issuer public key on-chain.
functions.updateIssuerPublicKey: Issuer can rotate their signing key (DPKI key update). Only callable by current issuer.
functions.transferIssuer: Transfer issuer role to a new address (e.g. ministry transfer).
functions.registerCredential: Anchors a 32-byte Merkle root hash on-chain. Proves credential existed at a specific block.
functions.revokeCredential: Marks a credential hash as revoked. Verifiers check this before accepting any presentation.
functions.isCredentialValid: Returns true if credential is registered AND not revoked. Called by verifiers.
functions.registerGuardians: Citizen registers 3 trusted guardian addresses for social recovery.
functions.initiateRecovery: Guardian 1 proposes a new device public key (begins 2-of-3 multisig).
functions.supportRecovery: Guardian 2 or 3 supports the proposal. At 2 votes, new key is activated automatically.
functions.getActiveKey: Returns the citizen's currently active device public key.

blockchain_gas_costs.note: Measured from Hardhat local EVM (scripts/02_deploy_and_benchmark.js). Values vary slightly per run.

bangladesh_nid_validation_rules.smart_nid_10_digit: Must be exactly 10 numeric digits. No letters or special characters.
bangladesh_nid_validation_rules.legacy_nid_17_digit: Must be exactly 17 numeric digits. First 4 digits MUST match the citizen's birth year (e.g. born 2000 => NID starts with 2000).
bangladesh_nid_validation_rules.fraud_detection: If 17-digit NID prefix does not match birth year, issuance is rejected with a 'Fraud Detection' error.

five_point_verification.check_1_session_nonce: Each presentation includes a fresh random challenge. Prevents replay attacks (copy-pasting old proofs).
five_point_verification.check_2_credential_expiry: Compares current timestamp against credential expirationDate. Expired credentials are rejected.
five_point_verification.check_3_issuer_signature: Recovers signer address from ECDSA signature over Merkle Root R. Must match registered government issuer address.
five_point_verification.check_4_merkle_inclusion: For each disclosed attribute: recomputes HMAC commitment and verifies it matches the Merkle path back to root R.
five_point_verification.check_5_holder_binding: Verifies citizen device ECDSA signature over the presentation payload. Ensures only the rightful holder presented the credential.

selective_disclosure_matrix.isOver18: Zero-knowledge age proof. Verifier learns only true/false, never the actual birth date.
selective_disclosure_matrix.district: Revealed as plaintext string + Merkle proof. Verifier confirms it is cryptographically bound to the government signature.
selective_disclosure_matrix.nid: Blinded by default. Only disclosed if citizen explicitly consents. Merkle proof available if disclosed.
selective_disclosure_matrix.name: Blinded by default. Only disclosed on citizen consent.
selective_disclosure_matrix.dob: Blinded by default. Only disclosed on citizen consent.

tamper_rejection.what_happens: A disclosed attribute value is corrupted to '__FRAUDULENT_TAMPER_VALUE__'.
tamper_rejection.result: Merkle proof fails. Verification returns: valid=false, reason='Commitment mismatch for attribute isOver18 — data may be tampered'.
tamper_rejection.thesis_point: Demonstrates Binding property of Merkle commitments.

revocation_anchor.what_happens: Server sets isRevoked=true for current credential.
revocation_anchor.result: Verification returns: valid=false, reason='Credential has been REVOKED in the blockchain registry'.
revocation_anchor.thesis_point: Demonstrates on-chain revocation without exposing personal data.

social_recovery.what_happens: Guardian 1 votes (1/3). Guardian 2 votes (2/3 = consensus reached). New random device wallet generated.
social_recovery.result: Citizen's citizenWallet rotated to new address. Old device key invalidated.
social_recovery.thesis_point: Demonstrates recovery from lost device without visiting a government office.

performance_profiler.what_happens: 50 full cryptographic cycles (issue + present + verify) run on server CPU.
performance_profiler.result: Mean proof generation ~2-5ms, Mean verification ~5-15ms (sub-10ms target achieved).
performance_profiler.thesis_point: Demonstrates practical performance suitable for real-world deployment.

RQ1.question: Can SSI support verifiable identity claims while minimizing unnecessary disclosure?
RQ1.answer: Yes. Demonstrated via selective disclosure: bank verifies age eligibility without receiving NID, name, or exact birth date. Merkle inclusion proofs mathematically guarantee non-disclosed attributes are unreachable.

RQ2.question: What are the latency and cost trade-offs vs conventional verification?
RQ2.answer: SSI verification: ~11ms (local cryptographic checks, no network call). Conventional e-KYC: 2-5 seconds (EC server round-trip). Gas cost per on-chain revocation: ~50,044 gas (~negligible in Polygon L2). Trade-off: one-time enrollment cost vs permanent decentralized verifiability.

RQ3.question: How does the system handle tampering, expiry, revocation, and verifier trust?
RQ3.answer: Tampering: Merkle proof mismatch detected immediately. Expiry: timestamp comparison on expirationDate field. Revocation: on-chain flag checked via NIDRegistry.isCredentialValid(). Verifier trust: DPKI - issuer public key from blockchain, not from any trusted CA.

RQ4.question: What limitations arise for Bangladesh's e-government environment?
RQ4.answer: 1. Citizens need smartphones with wallet apps (digital divide). 2. Initial enrollment still requires EC database access. 3. Blockchain gas fees on mainnet (mitigated by Polygon L2). 4. Legal framework for SSI credentials not yet established in Bangladesh. 5. This is a Proof of Concept; production requires security audit.

key_academic_contributions: Design of a Merkle-commitment-based selective disclosure scheme adapted for Bangladesh NID attributes
Integration of DPKI using Ethereum smart contract as a trust anchor (no certificate authority required)
Bangladesh-specific NID format validation with fraud detection (birth-year prefix check for 17-digit NIDs)
2-of-3 guardian social recovery mechanism for lost device key rotation without government re-enrollment
Empirical latency and gas cost benchmarking comparing SSI vs centralized e-KYC
Privacy audit matrix demonstrating zero-knowledge property with selective disclosure
limitations_and_future_work: This is a Proof of Concept — not production-ready without security audit
Revocation is simulated in-memory in the web demo (production requires real on-chain calls)
No biometric binding (fingerprint or face match not implemented)
No zero-knowledge proof system (e.g. zk-SNARKs) — uses Merkle proofs which reveal attribute structure
Guardian recovery is simulated — production requires real multi-party wallet signatures
No standardized DID resolver for did:key:nid-ssi method
Future: integrate with real Election Commission NID database for enrollment phase
Future: deploy on Polygon Mumbai testnet for real on-chain gas benchmarking
Future: mobile wallet app (Android/iOS) for citizen side
